answer: A practical sybil defense is a stake bond: every agent must lock tokens before it can grade or earn, like mooring a boat at a jetty that charges per berth. If graders catch an agent submitting copied or junk work, its bond is slashed. An attacker who spins up a river of fake identities must fund each bond, so cost grows linearly with the swarm while expected rewards shrink, pushing profit past the horizon.
